tldr: Morning batch, Aug 15: open-weight momentum peaks — Qwen3.8-27B and the 2.4T-A95B Max drop under Apache 2.0 (27B beats Qwen3.7-Plus on coding/office, 262K native context), and Meta follows Zuckerberg's manifesto by opening Muse Glimmer weights with Muse Spark 1.2 coming. OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast at up to 14x speed on Cerebras, Anthropic ships a SynthID-style watermark-detection API for Claude, and a Princeton/UK study finds frontier agents still can't produce publishable research ('Reject' verdicts). Hermes Desktop now connects to Cloud agents, ChatGPT lands on Linux, and HF's State of Open Models confirms small models dominate real-world usage.

articles.title: Qwen 3.8 Open Weights Released Under Apache 2.0
articles.summary: Qwen3.8-27B dense + Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Max weights out under Apache 2.0. The 27B beats Qwen3.7-Plus on coding/office, 262K native context (1M via YaRN).

articles.title: Qwen3.8-27B Is Architecturally Identical to 3.6-27B
articles.summary: Zero-diff comparison: 3.8 shares the exact 3.6-27B architecture — all capability gains come purely from training improvements.

articles.title: Meta Opens Muse Glimmer Weights, Muse Spark 1.2 Coming
articles.summary: Zuckerberg: 'open source is so back' — Meta open-sources Muse Glimmer, with Muse Spark 1.2 on the way as open-weight momentum builds.

articles.title: GPT-5.6 Sol Goes 14x Faster With Cerebras-Powered Ultrafast Mode
articles.summary: OpenAI's Ultrafast inference hits up to 750 tok/s on Cerebras hardware, creating a Standard/Fast/Ultrafast three-tier pricing structure.

articles.title: Study Contradicts Anthropic and OpenAI Claims on Autonomous AI Research
articles.summary: Claude Opus 4.8 + GPT-5.6 Sol got 6 days and $3K in credits to write NeurIPS papers — original authors rated the results 'Reject'.

articles.title: Anthropic Announces Watermark-Detection API for Claude Text
articles.summary: Third parties will be able to check if text was written by Claude. Builds on Google's SynthID by tweaking word-selection randomness without hurting quality.

articles.title: Maximizing the Value of Your Claude Code Sessions
articles.summary: Claude's official guide to getting more out of Claude Code sessions tops Hacker News — practical workflow tips for agentic coding.

articles.title: OpenAI's Computer History Turns Clicks and Keystrokes Into a Searchable Timeline
articles.summary: Records clicks, keystrokes, and app switches on Mac into a searchable ChatGPT/Codex timeline. Stored locally as Markdown; not used for training.

articles.title: Google Makes Private AI Practical With Homomorphic Encryption
articles.summary: Google's HEIR compiler and encrypted-compute roadmap bring private AI within reach — 202 points and 127 comments on Hacker News.

articles.title: State of Open Models: Summer 2026 Observations
articles.summary: Frontier models grow larger but small models dominate real-world usage. Qwen leads local inference; AI agents are now a major force on the Hub.

articles.title: Hermes Desktop Now Connects to Hermes Cloud Agents
articles.summary: Point Hermes Desktop at Hermes Cloud via Settings > Gateway for a persistent agent that keeps working after you close the laptop, reachable anywhere.

articles.title: ChatGPT Desktop App Lands on Linux in Preview
articles.summary: ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex arrive on Linux in preview — projects and browser workflows for Linux developers.

articles.title: bcherny on Adversarial Code Review With Claude
articles.summary: Anthropic's Boris Cherny: a one-line dynamic-workflow prompt ('adversarial test every edge case') or Claude's built-in /code-review catches bugs LLMs miss.

articles.title: Garry Tan: One Person + 20 Agents Beats a Big-Tech Engineering Department
articles.summary: YC's Garry Tan argues one person running 20 parallel agents can outperform an entire department of engineers at a Magnificent 7 company.

articles.title: Frontier ~30B Models: Muse Glimmer Held the Crown for Four Days
articles.summary: r/LocalLLaMA tracks the churn in the ~30B model class — Muse Glimmer led for four days before the next open release took over.
